items.title: vercel-labs/agent-desktop
items.summary: agent-desktop, developed by Vercel Labs, is a command-line interface (CLI) that allows AI agents to read and manage desktop applications via the operating system's accessibility tree. Written in Rust, this tool aims to improve the computer use capabilities of agents.

snapshot.description: Computer use CLI for AI agents. Computer use for AI agents: read and operate desktop apps through the OS accessibility tree.

items.title: D4Vinci/Scrapling
items.summary: Scrapling, a Python-based web scraping framework, aims to manage all processes from single requests to comprehensive crawling operations. This tool offers developers an end-to-end solution for data collection tasks.

snapshot.description: 🕷️ The BEST Web Scraping framework that handles everything from a single request to a full-scale crawl! Don't be shy, join here: https://discord.gg/EMgGbDceNQ and follow here for daily tips and tricks: https://x.com/Scrapling_dev

items.title: JustVugg/colibri
items.summary: JustVugg/colibri is a C engine that enables running frontier Mixture of Experts (MoE) models on existing hardware with an architecture where experts are streamed from disk. The software aims to make large-scale models available with minimal infrastructure without requiring any dependencies.

snapshot.description: Run frontier MoE models on hardware you already own — pure C, zero deps, experts streamed from disk. Tiny engine, immense model. 🐦

items.title: max-sixty/worktrunk
items.summary: Worktrunk is a command-line interface (CLI) developed in Rust that simplifies Git worktree management. The software is designed to allow AI agents to execute multiple workflows in parallel.

snapshot.description: Worktrunk is a CLI for Git worktree management, designed for parallel AI agent workflows. Worktrunk is a CLI for git worktree management, designed for running AI agents in parallel.

items.title: paperclipai/paperclip
items.summary: Paperclip is an open-source orchestration platform developed to manage AI agents in the workplace. It allows teams to coordinate multiple AI agents together.

snapshot.description: The open-source app everyone uses to manage agents at work. Open-source orchestration for teams of AI agents.

items.title: karpathy/nanochat
items.summary: karpathy/nanochat is an experimental software framework developed for training large language models (LLMs) that can run on a single graphics processing unit (GPU). Covering tokenization, pre-training, fine-tuning, evaluation, and inference processes, this project offers developers a minimal and modifiable structure.

snapshot.description: The best ChatGPT that $100 can buy. nanochat is the simplest experimental harness for training LLMs. It is designed to run on a single GPU node, the code is minimal/hackable, and it covers all major LLM stages including tokenization, pretraining, finetuning, evaluation, and inference.

items.title: p-e-w/heretic
items.summary: p-e-w/heretic is a software tool that allows for training-free modifications to language models. It enables users to remove censorship, reduce unnecessary content (slop), and decrease the tendency for sycophancy in AI models.

snapshot.description: Training-free language model modification: Remove censorship, suppress slop, reduce sycophancy, and more. Remove censorship, suppress slop, reduce sycophancy, and more. All in an afternoon, on your gaming PC.

items.title: Astra can read and write weights to improve Qwen
items.summary: Astra offers the ability to improve large language models (LLMs) like Qwen by directly reading and writing the weights of AI models. This method demonstrates that AI models can perform operations on neural network weights more successfully than humans or traditional algorithms.

snapshot.description: We find that frontier LLMs are surprisingly good at natively reading and writing neural network weights, well past what we’d expect from humans or conventional algorithms.

items.title: WTF Ubuntu?
items.summary: The article written by Chalmovsky criticizes some configuration choices and technical changes affecting the user experience in recent versions of the Ubuntu operating system. The author questions the unexpected situations encountered regarding the system's operation and the impact of these changes on users.

items.summary: Subvocal is developing smart glasses that allow users to command their computers using only lip movements without making a sound. This technology offers a private and fast method of communication by converting silently spoken words into text.

items.title: Ubuntu still has not released patch for Linux 0day RCE in almost 3 weeks
items.summary: Ubuntu has not yet released a patch for a critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability with a 9.8 CVSS score in versions 22.04, 24.04, and 26.04. The vulnerability in question has been awaiting a fix for operating system kernels for approximately three weeks.

snapshot.description: No patched kernels are available yet for 22.04, 24.04, or 26.04 despite a CVSS 9.8 rating.

items.title: Democratizing Robot-Use Agents: A Unified Harness with Open Models
items.summary: Developed for Robot-use Agents (RUAs), uni-robot-agent offers a unified infrastructure aimed at making robotics research more accessible with open-weight models. The Qwen3.8-Flash-Next model demonstrates competitive performance, surpassing the GPT-6 Astra-RoboProbe result in the RoboDojo test without the need for custom data inputs.

snapshot.description: Robot-use Agents (RUAs) have shown promising zero-shot manipulation capabilities, but reliance on frontier, proprietary models limits research into further training. To democratize RUA research, we introduce uni-robot-agent, a unified harness for competitive open-weight robot use that supports further training. items.title: NorthCUA Technical Report: Turbocharging Computer-Use Agents through Experience at Scale
items.summary: NorthCUA is an integrated system aimed at enhancing the performance of computer-use AI agents in complex software tasks through scalable experiences. By executing various tasks via an Experience Flywheel, the system records long-term interactions to create verified solution paths.

snapshot.description: Scaling computer-use agents from individual actions to complex software work requires experience that connects decisions to complete outcomes. We present NorthCUA, an integrated system for turbocharging computer-use agents through experience at scale. Its Experience Flywheel supplies diverse executable tasks to the NorthCUA Harness, which sustains long interactions, records decisions, and checks task outcomes. items.title: Wave Forcing: Towards Speed-of-Light Streaming Video Generation
items.summary: Wave Forcing is a method that designs video generation, training, and execution processes together to produce continuous video output. It aims to address efficiency issues seen in current methods and the loss of image quality in long-duration videos.

snapshot.description: Real-time long-video generation requires continuous output with consistent appearance and natural motion. Existing chunk-wise autoregressive methods face challenges in both generation efficiency and long-video quality: serialized denoising and history-cache refresh require two forward passes even with one-step denoising, and longer rollouts can degrade quality and cause camera drift. items.title: TinyAstral: Transferring Self-Evolving Harnesses to Tiny Generalist Manipulation Agents
items.summary: TinyAstral is a two-stage method aimed at transferring auxiliary structures (harnesses) such as tools, feedback, and memory—possessed by large AI models—to smaller robotic agents. This approach aims to transport the capabilities acquired by large models through recursive self-improvement to compact agents that require low processing power.

snapshot.description: Robot agents built on vision-language models depend on both the planner and its harness: the tools, feedback, memory, and recovery logic around it. Can improvements to a large teacher's harness be carried into a compact agent with lower inference compute cost? We present TinyAstral, a two-stage approach. items.title: Lost in Recovery: Demystifying Recovery Behavior of Computer-Use Agents via Goal-Oriented Action Replay
items.summary: The article shared by Hugging Face examines the error accumulation and recovery difficulties encountered by computer-use AI agents in long-term tasks. The study aims to improve the post-error recovery processes of these agents using a goal-oriented action replay method.

snapshot.description: Recent advances in large (vision) language models have enabled computer-use agents that automate digital workflows via fine-grained keyboard and mouse operations. However, such agents remain fragile in long-horizon settings, where errors accumulate and executed actions leave unintended side effects, making the ability to recover from failures critical.
